Consternant. 
Ce post Reddit d&#39;un ancien AM de Google traduit parfaitement ce que je ressens quand je vois l&#39;évolution de Google Ads en 10 ans :pray: :pray: . 

Rien à ajouter.

𝐑𝐞𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐝𝐮 𝐭𝐞𝐱𝐭𝐞:point_down: 

I was fired as a Google rep because...

:point_right: I refused to lie about the Automatically applied recommendation which automatically changed your account. But Google saw that as a missed opportunity.

:point_right: I refused to force struggling business owners to increase their budgets. Google saw that as a failure to achieve.

:point_right: I refused to force a Well-functioning high CTR with high Conversion rate, manual CPC campaign to a smart bidding strategy. Google saw that as a lack of product understand.

:point_right: The majority of the major partner agencies with $20,000+ accounts would only consult me and ignore my team because their agency CEO knew my name and only trusted me. Google saw that as nothing.

:point_right: I refused to start the Pmax campaign for non-merchant accounts that were only lead-based. Those accounts don&#39;t need Pmax. Google saw that as a lack of ambition to improve accounts.

:point_right: I refused to pitch the idea of broad match keywords when exact match keywords are bringing results. Google saw that as a lack of motive to expand accounts and improve them.

:point_right: I would sit there as a full stack rep and make conversation actions, create codes for data layer pushing, and make sure clients were getting the best conversion data to train the ML and AI bidding strategy. I was told that&#39;s not my job.

:point_right: I refused to harass and spam call clients in my book who did not want to meet with me and had already told me so. Google saw that as a lack of effort.

You, agency folks, are not going anywhere. Clients need you as a shield first. | 23 comments on LinkedIn
